A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SimulMEGA and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison of the complete work.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech translation and TTS evaluations, ablation experiments, deployment latency measurements, and translation case studies in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix latency measurements and case studies.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objectives, routing policy, and TTS adaptation are retained. The corrected prefix-expert equation matches the prefix input already shown in v1 Figure 2(b), so it does not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six-language speech translation coverage, CoVoST2 and FLEURS evaluations, English/Chinese TTS benchmarks, and appendix deployment and case-study scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the Seamless family, Wait-K, DiG-SST, EDATT, AlignATT, CosyVoice2 variants, NAST-S2S, and StreamSpeech. Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the training budgets, model configurations, and evaluation procedures; Appendix B retains the baseline settings and threshold grids. Appendix D still tests two 20–30-second samples for each of four translation directions.

E4.justification: The noise-scale, score-normalization, and training-loss ablations in Section 4.3 are unchanged. Appendices C, D, and F retain the same computation-overhead analysis, deployment latency analysis, and translation case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing averaging practices and Appendix D qualification that latency measurements are rough estimates remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted curves, and case-study outputs are unchanged, including Appendix Tables 4–5. For example, Table 1 retains SimulMEGA-S2T's CoVoST2 X-EN BLEU of 36.9, and Table 2 retains SimulMEGA-TTS's LibriSpeech WER of 2.54.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the prefix-expert cross-attention formula: its key and value projections use h_prefix in v2 instead of h_offline in v1. This repairs the mathematical specification to agree with the existing architecture diagram; the other equations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning unsupervised MoE policy learning, multilingual quality–latency trade-offs, and applicability to streaming TTS.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds history selection alongside sliding windows as a possible future approach to continuous generation beyond the 30-second input limit. This is a limited extension of the limitations discussion; existing result interpretations and stated failure conditions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SimulMEGA code-repository link in a page-1 footnote, supplying access information absent from v1. The implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and deployment details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 49 cited works are retained. Reference text moves across page boundaries, but the paper's relationship to prior research and novelty positioning do not change.

P1.justification: v2 expands the institutional affiliation, replaces the preprint notice with a NeurIPS 2025 venue notice, and adds Section 6, Acknowledgment. Apart from brief local edits, the research narrative and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation and added code footnote reflow the opening pages, while the acknowledgment shifts the references. Figures 1–8 have identical embedded images, and the table structures and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves technical consistency by correcting the prefix-expert equation to match the existing architecture, and improves reproducibility documentation by providing a code location. These are useful, limited gains; the experimental evidence and conclusions are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
